summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with left flank pain, fevers, and decreased output from his left nephrostomy tube, found to be occluded. He underwent successful PCN tube exchange with drainage of infected fluid. Cultures grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, and he was started on IV daptomycin for a planned 14-day course. His chronic kidney disease remained stable, but he developed hyperkalemia (K 6.1), which he declined treatment for. He also acknowledged recent cocaine use related to grief over a friend’s death. Despite medical advice, he eloped on hospital day 8, having completed only part of his antibiotic course. He was alert and stable at the time, with functioning PCN and improved pain, but was strongly advised to follow up with urology, nephrology, and outpatient support.
